cards.explanation: The answer is the Philistines, friends. The writer says war broke out with them at Gezer (1 Chronicles 20:4). That answer is sitting right there in the first verse.
The answer is True! Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai at Gezer (1 Chronicles 20:4). Sippai was a descendant of the Rephaim. The text says the Philistines were subdued.

The answer is subdued, friends. After Sippai was killed, the Philistines were subdued (1 Chronicles 20:4). That means they were brought low and their fight was held down. Think of dough after a good press, all the puff gone out of it.
The answer is Goliath the Gittite! Lahmi was the brother of Goliath the Gittite (1 Chronicles 20:5). Elhanan son of Jair is the one who killed Lahmi. Now that's a famous name to find in this verse.
The answer is six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, friends (1 Chronicles 20:6). The text also says he was a man of great stature. It adds that he too was descended from Rapha.

The answer is twenty-four, bakers! Six fingers on each hand is twelve, and six toes on each foot is another twelve (1 Chronicles 20:6). Add them up and the text says "…twenty-four in all." Good math to all of you.

The answer is Jonathan son of Shimei! When the man at Gath taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David's brother Shimei killed him (1 Chronicles 20:7). Shimei was David's brother, so Jonathan is David's nephew. A family member took care of it, and that's the whole story.

The answers are David and servants, friends. The text says these descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants (1 Chronicles 20:8). Sibbecai, Elhanan and Jonathan are each named in this passage as killing one of these men. David and his servants, together, are who the verse names.
